{{short description|American economist and mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''William R. Zame''' is an American economist and mathematician, and distinguished professor of economics. Dr Zame earned his PhD degree at [[Tulane University]]. Before joining the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1991, he held appointments in the Mathematics Departments of [[Rice University]], [[Tulane University]] and [[State University of New York at Buffalo|the State University of New York at Buffalo]], and in the Economics and Mathematics Departments at The [[Johns Hopkins University]]. His research areas are [[Experimental economics|Experimental Economics]], [[Finance]], [[Game theory|Game Theory]], [[Microeconomics|Microeconomic]]. Research topics include the impact of culture on economic outcomes in diverse societies, [https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/asymmetricinformation.asp informational asymmetries] in macroeconomics, [[Experimental finance|experimental financial markets]], and a number of topics in [[machine learning]]. He is currently Co-Editor of Economic Theory and Associate Editor of Theoretical Economics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.econ.ucla.edu/zame/ |title=William Zame |publisher=ucla.edu |accessdate=February 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://economics.ucla.edu/person/william-r-zame/ |title=William R. Zame |date=21 October 2016 |publisher=ucla.edu |accessdate=February 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=aHa6fz4AAAAJ&hl=en |title=William Zame |accessdate=February 27, 2017}}</ref>
